body:
## Where the input path actually spends device time

The headline table in the PR body is process wall; this is the breakdown under it.
One Nsight capture per arm per variant, device intervals only.

![device ingest stages](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/7b47c18cefbcc3c754c0df660ce3b2ceb134fee0/docs/input_backends/charts/ingest-stages.png)

| input | arm | route | deflate decode | Adler-32 | convert+gain+sum | H2D copy | ingest total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| uint8 Deflate, 24f | main | float | — | — | 2.8 ms | 211.2 ms | **214.0 ms** |
| | branch | nvcomp | 24.7 ms | 1.1 ms | 1.8 ms | 15.6 ms | **43.2 ms** |
| uint8 Deflate, 48f | main | float | — | — | 6.5 ms | 499.9 ms | **506.4 ms** |
| | branch | nvcomp | 49.2 ms | 2.1 ms | 3.7 ms | 19.3 ms | **74.3 ms** |
| uint16 Deflate, 8 rows/strip | main | compact | — | — | 3.9 ms | 103.2 ms | **107.1 ms** |
| | branch | nvcomp | 21.4 ms | 1.8 ms | 2.0 ms | 16.6 ms | **41.8 ms** |
| uint16 Deflate, 1 row/strip *(null)* | main | nvcomp | 22.9 ms | 1.9 ms | 1.9 ms | 16.2 ms | **42.9 ms** |
| | branch | nvcomp | 22.9 ms | 1.9 ms | 2.0 ms | 16.9 ms | **43.7 ms** |

Three things a wall-clock number cannot show:

* **The GPU Deflate decode is cheap relative to the copy it removes.** 24.7 ms of
  decode replaces a 211.2 ms copy; the whole ingest drops 80%, and the decode is
  then the largest piece of what is left.
* **Adler-32 recomputation costs 1.1–2.1 ms per movie.** That is the price of
  keeping the integrity check that handing nvCOMP a raw Deflate stream discards.
  It is not where the time goes, and it is not a reason to drop it.
* **The alignment, FFT and dose work after the ingest is 104 ms (24 frames) /
  230 ms (48) in every arm.** That is the internal control: these columns are the
  only thing that moved.

### Bytes, which are contention-immune where the times are not

![host-to-device bytes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/7b47c18cefbcc3c754c0df660ce3b2ceb134fee0/docs/input_backends/charts/h2d-bytes.png)

The three unchanged-route variants are **byte-identical across arms**, which is
what makes the others attributable. Read the time column of the null rows as the
spread of this measurement on a shared box: uint16 LZW copies the same 751 MB in
100.5 ms on one arm and 115.6 ms on the other.

### Residency and per-movie wall

![host resident set](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/7b47c18cefbcc3c754c0df660ce3b2ceb134fee0/docs/input_backends/charts/host-rss.png)

![per-movie wall](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/7b47c18cefbcc3c754c0df660ce3b2ceb134fee0/docs/input_backends/charts/per-movie-wall.png)

### Provenance

The measured binaries are this branch **minus the last commit** (the TIMING
stage tag). Compiling `motioncorr_runner.cpp` from both trees at the measured
configuration gives 161,492 assembly lines each, differing only in immediate
constants — string-table offsets and timer ordinals shifted by one added
`Timer::setNew`. No instruction is added to the per-movie path.

Charts are self-contained SVG built from the committed JSON under
`docs/input_backends/data/` by `docs/input_backends/harness/build_charts.py`;
no plotting dependency, so they rebuild anywhere.

### Still UNRUN

Host-side stage split (LZW/Deflate CPU decode vs float materialisation) from a
`TIMING=ON` pair — queued behind two other sessions on the shared box. It is
the one part of the data-loading story these charts do not yet separate.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Review note: **request changes before merge**. There is a large-strip Adler-32 correctness bug in the current CUDA checksum kernel: the weighted term accumulates in uint64 and only reduces modulo 65521 at the end, so it can overflow for sufficiently large valid strips. A 512 MiB all-0xff strip gives the correct/streaming zlib Adler value 0x2a2a3c03, while the current uint64 accumulation model gives 0x645a3c03. The safe worst-case strip length is only about 380,368,696 bytes (~362.75 MiB). Please do bounded modular reduction during accumulation (preferred) or prove/enforce a safe admitted-length bound, and add a large-length checksum test. Separately, this PR expands the nvCOMP trust boundary beyond #137; healthy-output checks do not establish malformed-input safety, so keep the policy/recovery work in #134 explicit. The reported speedups are promising, but should not be added on top of #137 because this branch is stacked on it.

body:
Additional source review at7b47c18c: after nvcompBatchedDeflateDecompressAsync, adler32StripsKernel reads each declared strip before host status/actual-length acceptance. A failed/short chunk can therefore be checksummed before it is accepted, and the first diagnostic can become Adler mismatch rather than the decoder failure. This is #134 item3, separate from the large-strip arithmetic finding already posted by the other reviewer.

Small repair: gate checksum input reads on per-chunk success AND exactdecodedlength (device checks or checkedstatus/length before launch); preserve deterministicfirst-failure status and reject the batch before convert/gain/sum. Power failedstatus and shortlength controls against the actualkernel/caller boundary, with healthycontrols and no acceptedjointSTAR/product afterfailedattempt. Keep malformed-stream library execution safety separate from post-decode checksum integrity. No newGPUnegative or universal safetyclaim from this review. Do not duplicate137's unaffected host-codec acceptance.

## Host-side stage split — the half the earlier charts left as a residual

`TIMING=ON` builds of both arms, median of 3 repetitions, whole-run stage
totals. **These walls are not comparable with the production figures** — an
instrumented build is a different binary — but the stage attribution is what
this is for.

![host ingest stages](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/6ccaaf5b5bd7788fe7ad8c0fd0e96c1bb5bc5bc2/docs/input_backends/charts/host-stages.png)

| variant | arm | route | host decode | device ingest | gain + sum + upload | total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| uint8 LZW, 24f x 6 | main | float | 2.19 s | — | 1.41 s | **3.60 s** |
| | branch | compact | 1.83 s | — | 0.45 s | **2.28 s** |
| uint8 Deflate, 24f x 6 | main | float | 1.94 s | — | 1.55 s | **3.48 s** |
| | branch | nvcomp | — | 0.69 s | — | **0.69 s** |
| uint16 Deflate rps8, 24f x 6 | main | compact | 1.61 s | — | 0.72 s | **2.34 s** |
| | branch | nvcomp | — | 0.72 s | — | **0.72 s** |
| uint16 LZW *(null)*, 24f x 6 | main | compact | 2.59 s | — | 0.73 s | **3.32 s** |
| | branch | compact | 2.57 s | — | 0.76 s | **3.33 s** |

* **The compact route splits its win across two stages.** uint8 LZW: host decode
  2.19 → 1.83 s (no longer materialising floats) *and* gain-and-sum 1.41 → 0.45 s
  (device widens, upload is a quarter of the bytes). Neither alone is the change.
* **nvCOMP deletes both stages.** uint8 Deflate goes from 1.94 s of host decode
  plus 1.55 s of gain-and-sum to one 0.69 s device ingest — **5.0x less host time
  on the input path**.
* **Null control flat**: 3.32 vs 3.33 s on the unchanged compact route.
* `main` predates the device-ingest timer, so where main itself takes nvCOMP that
  stage is untagged and reads zero. That row is marked on the chart, not compared.

### This also replaces an inference with a measurement

The remaining LZW cost is now attributed, not derived: on the compact route the
host decode is **0.305 s/movie (uint8)** and **0.428 s/movie (uint16)**. That is
the work a GPU LZW decoder would remove, and it is now the measured budget in
#141 rather than the estimate I opened that issue with.

With this, every queued item from the PR body is closed except the pinned
`--ingest` contract matrix and the MRC route witness, both of which ran in
campaigns 6–7 and are being folded in next.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Everything listed as UNRUN is now run

### Pinned-route contract — 30/30 cells as specified

`--ingest {nvcomp,compact,float}` must fail a movie that cannot take the named
route rather than quietly using another. Ten variants, three pinned modes each:

| variant | nvcomp | compact | float |
|---|---|---|---|
| uint16 Deflate 1 / 8 / 512 rows per strip | OK | OK | OK |
| uint8 Deflate 1 / 16 rows per strip | OK | OK | OK |
| uint16 LZW · uint8 LZW 1 / 3837 rows per strip | **REFUSED** | OK | OK |
| uint16 Deflate predictor 2 · uint16 uncompressed | **REFUSED** | OK | OK |

Every refusal is a codec or predictor nvCOMP genuinely cannot take, and each
still has both host routes. No variant silently changed route under a pin — so
the route matrix in the PR body is about eligibility, not defaults.

### Selected frames and grouping — 28/28 PASS

`--first_frame_sum`, `--last_frame_sum`, `--group_frames` and all three
together, on the uint16 Deflate reference and both uint8 variants, both arms,
seven option sets. The route does not change which frames are used, how they
are numbered, or what the dose weighting does.

My earlier run of this gate reported FAIL on every row. That verdict was
unreadable, not a failure: the comparator was invoked without
`--allow-added-log-line`, so a route change showed up as six differing `.log`
files while every MRC and STAR was identical. Re-run through the declaring
wrapper, it passes.

### MRC route witness

An MRC movie must take the float route — the compact gate requires a `tif`
format and the nvCOMP gate opens with `TIFFOpen`. Now observed rather than read
from the source: `--ingest_witness` records `float`.

### Added to the limitations

**No GPU LZW.** nvCOMP has no LZW codec — verified against the installed 5.3
library, zero LZW symbols. LZW keeps its host decode, measured at 0.305 s/movie
(uint8) and 0.428 s/movie (uint16). nvTIFF is the only supported way to move it
and is scoped separately in #141 with that figure as its budget; nothing here
installed or ran it.

---

Nothing from the original deliverable list is outstanding. Remaining known
limitations are in `docs/input_backends/RESULTS.md` §8 and are properties of the
work, not gaps in it.

Corrected native acceptance completed on VMGPU0/CPUs96–103, payload3026917 (actual /proc PID/start666603229 and /usr/bin/bash recorded), CUDA12.8.61/nvCOMP5.3.0.16. Clean acceptance composition50a59b5 keeps original production arithmetic from75c8, adds only reviewed875857f diagnostic-surface control. **CPU34/34, CUDA-noNV42/42, CUDA-NV45/45 PASS, none skipped.** Actual512MiB arithmetic/status/length selected positives pass; three actual kernel mutants plus real caller diagnostic-order mutant fail as intended and restored controls pass. Source/binary/input/SDK hashes and exit0/released GPU retained.

Original75c8 NV44/45 FAIL remains retained: correct rejection was logged per-movie while the test searched only process output. Host gate controls and native replay certify the repair rather than suppressing that failure. Earlier SCARF retries were cancelled before allocation.

**Still HOLD for product promotion:** Issue134 malformed-Deflate decoder trust policy is unresolved. Healthy decoder input plus inaccessible direct-kernel fault controls do not establish malformed decoder safety. No current-main merge, throughput, scientific accuracy or broad input-support claim.

Review: split the useful correctness repair from the wider nvCOMP admission policy. Current main still benefits from the modular Adler-32 fix and from accepting decoder status/actual length before consuming/checksumming output; that narrow repair has discriminating 512 MiB and caller-order evidence. The wider 8/16-bit/RowsPerStrip promotion should remain held behind #134 because post-decode checks do not establish malformed-Deflate safety. Also preserve process output before any harness-side missing-log rejection so early failures remain diagnosable.

Report/discussion triage at head `875857f1ba3390c53cdf97f68afaa2a1f1e4832b`, with release context from current main `cb3699ac` and #198.

Do not merge this historical stacked branch. The later current-pipeline port #206 is explicitly parked under T1, independently of D1. Current #198 also supersedes the old 'trust decision unresolved' wording: D1 selected a documented trusted immutable-input precondition, which is not a malformed-input safety proof.

The original format matrix consists of tutorial re-encodes, and its 48-frame cases repeat the same 24 frames. Its large speed percentages therefore do not establish a benefit for deposited LZW collections or today's pipeline. #206 adds the decisive tall-strip limitation and confirms no real corpus beneficiary for this widening. The narrow #151 checksum/status-order repair has already been separated; any future widening should start from current main, preserve #217's arithmetic checks, justify an admission floor and requalify actual affected data.

No new build, benchmark or native test was run in this review; this is not a full source audit.
